headline: Hex has not yet released the new client with its new registry signing key, and has not said whether account data was taken.
summary: Re-read Hex's incident post (s001, Nov 24, unchanged) and blog index: newest post is still the incident post, with no release announcement. Hex's install list still tops out at Hex 2.7.0, a file last changed Nov 6, before the incident; the new signing key (q007) has not shipped as far as public pages show. Nothing new on account data (q004), the attacker (q005) or affected organisations (q006); SEC EDGAR search (Nov 17-28) found none. The maintainers' forum thread (s004) adds re-authentication advice for OAuth errors after the credential rotation. Theory sweep: Hacker News threads on the post have no comments.
author: Research agent

headline: Hex says an attacker ran commands on six hex.pm servers on Nov 23 and may have read account data; it asks users to change passwords.
summary: New incident page. Read Hex's own incident post in full (s001, Tier 1, Nov 24) and its About and home pages (s002, s005); The Hacker News (s003, Tier 2, Nov 25) adds the clarification that download-only users have nothing to reset, otherwise repeats the post. Main answer Confirmed and answer_group hack-stated: Hex itself says an attacker got in. incident_type breach: account data may have been read. No service: nothing went down. Size Large: Hex serves the Elixir and Erlang ecosystem worldwide; size_basis says what is actually known. Hex's no-tampering and API-key judgements are its word alone, so Reported. Supplier question (q006): Hex's site, SEC filings Nov 20-26 and news reporting name no customer and no affected organisation; recorded as c013, Not established. Theory sweep: Hacker News threads had no comments; the Elixir Forum thread (s004, Tier 5) raised practical questions only, none by several commenters, so no rumor rows; Reddit could not be read. Picture: a screenshot of Hex's notice, with the byline and contact address hidden; Wikimedia Commons refused searches (429). Privacy check done: no staff, commenters or contacts named.
author: Research agent
